newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Sept 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Sept 6.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- AMEC SEEKS INTERNATIONAL PARTNERS FOR EXPANSION

Amec's chief executive Peter Mason warned yesterday that if the construction and engineering group want to secure meaningful future growth it will need to enter into international alliances. Mason was speaking after announcing Amec's best interim results for five years with pre-tax profits in the first half of this year doubled to 12.1 million stg.
-- HILLSDOWN HELD BACK BY BSE CRISIS

Hillsdown Holdings, the food group, yesterday announced profits badly dented by the crisis over BSE in British beef. But it added that strong market positions in other areas made it optimistic for the coming year. Profits from continuing operations rose from 56 million to 63.6 million stg in the first six months with pre-tax profits of 43.7 million stg.
-- WEAK DEMAND CUTS ARJO BACK TO 32 MILLION STG

Arjo Wiggins Appleton, the Anglo-French paper maker, saw pre-tax profits collapse to 32.3 million stg in the first half of this year from 135 million stg. It later said that widespread cost-cutting plans would be put in place in its declining carbonless paper business in Europe and America. The group blamed the tumble on weak demand and the fall in the price of pulp.
THE TIMES
-- HIGH STREET TRADE AT BEST LEVELS SINCE 1980S, SAYS CBI

The Confederation of British Industry said Britain's high streets are enjoying their best business since the late 1980s but added that Britain was not enjoying the same boom conditions as then and that calls for higher interest rates are unjustified.
-- SFO ON ALERT OVER MORGAN GRENFELL

An investigation may be launched by the Serious Fraud Office into the way in which 1.4 billion stg worth of investors money was managed by Morgan Grenfell. Investors withdrew 114 million stg from the three European Morgan Grenfell funds at the centre of the inquiry by City watchdogs the SFO. The SFO said that it had continued to monitor developments, but it had not yet been passed a case file.
-- GRANADA PLANS SPRING GROVE SALE FOR 136 MILLION STG

As part of its efforts to dispose of non-core businesses, Granada agreed to sell Spring Grove Services yesterday. Davis Service, a big operator in the linen rental and cleaning business is paying 136.5 million stg in cash for Spring Grove. It announced a one-for-three rights issue, raising 71.5 million stg, to help finance the deal.
THE GUARDIAN
-- C&G LEADS RETREAT FROM MORTGAGE DISCOUNT WAR

Cheltenham & Gloucester yesterday withdrew its discount mortgages, effectively pushing up the cost of a new home by up to 3 percent in the first year. C&G said its decision to end discounts had been partly caused by Bank of England and Building Society Commission concerns that young homeowners with big discounts might find it difficult meeting their repayments if interest rates rose sharply at the end of the discount period.
-- GRANDMET SELL-OFF MARKS END OF EUROPEAN HOPES

Grand Metropolitan, the food and drink group, yesterday signalled the end of ambitions to build a European food empire after selling the first of a string of weak food companies. GrandMet will receive 140 million stg from Campbell Soup for a German soup maker, Erasco. The group is looking for buyers for other national brands.
-- CAR INDUSTRY HITS BRAKES AFTER AUGUST EUPHORIA

Despite signs that individual car buyers are less interested in new P-registration cars, the motor industry recorded its second busiest month of car sales ever in August. The industry's euphoria that it was heading for more than two million car sales this year was lessened by claims that two thirds of new cars have faults because of poor quality control in the rush to meet August sales.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- LONDON FUNDS HIT AS OLIVETTI TEETERS

Olivetti, the Italian computer giant was on the brink of disaster last night after chief operating officer, Renzo Francesconi resigned on Wednesday night accusing the company of disguising the extent of its half-year losses. The Italian stock market regulators were forced to suspend Olivetti shares on the Milan bourse.
-- LONRHO HOTEL FLOAT ON ICE AS BUYERS NIBBLE

Lonrho put the planned flotation of its Metropole and Princess hotel chains on hold yesterday after the conglomerate said it had received approaches from a number of interested parties. The announcement just a day before Lonrho was due to publish a prospectus detailing an international share offer, has prompted analysts to speculate of potential bidders for the hotels.
-- FIRST-HALF SLIDE AT ROYAL & SUN ALLIANCE

The newly-merged composite insurer, Royal & Sun Alliance, yesterday reported a slide in first half pre-tax profits, but stated that it was still on target to achieve full integration of the two companies by 1998. The company expect to cut 175 million stg in annual costs by then, achieved mainly by making up to 5,000 staff redundant, mostly in the UK.
